newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt ends tighter, retail demand seen.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt ends tighter, retail demand seen.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds tightened a touch in active trading as solid retail demand kept players busy, high-grade traders said.
Spreads to U.S. Treasuries were seen tighter by one to two basis points across the baord, they added.
"We've seen a lot of solid retail interest at these levels," one high-grade trader said.
Another trader echoed the view: "It was very busy today...we've seen a lot of buyside interest. We saw more trades on the offering side of the market," he added.

Meanwhile, Philip Morris 7.20 percent paper tightened by about a basis point to trade at a spread of 71 basis points bid, 69 offer, while RJR Nabisco 8.75 percent debt was quoted at 185 basis points bid, 175 offer, traders said.
Despite busy secondary trading activity, the primary sector drew a lot of interest as sidelined debt issuers came back to market, traders said.
Investors hungry for corporate paper gobbled up Seagate Technology's $700 million debt offering, which was upped in size twice on Thursday to meet demand, traders said.
The initial Seagate deal, a $450 million three-part debt offering was upped in size to $500 million, followed by another increase to $700 million and the addition of a fourth tranche, dealers said.

The $200 million seven-year notes priced to yield 65 basis points, $200 million 10-year notes priced to yield 80 basis points, $200 million 40-year bonds priced to yield 88 basis points over its 12-year put, sources said.
The additional $100 million 20-year tranche was priced to yield 105 basis points over Treasuries, sources added.
Among other successful deals on Thursday was Corporacion Andina de Fomento's $150 million 10-year yankee issue which was more than three times oversubscribed, players said.
A second tranche of $50 million 20-year bonds priced at 91 basis points over Treasuries and was also oversubscribed, they added.
Turning to the high-yield sector, players said secondary trading activity picked up substantially with retail and gaming sector issues emerging as key gainers on the day.
In the retail sector, Penn Traffic 9.625 percent paper gained 2-3/4 points, erasing Wednesday's losses, traders said.
In the gaming sector, Harrah's Jazz recouped some of yesterday's losses, trading up 3/4 to 47-1/4 bid.
Also, Pioneer Finance debt gained one point, following a three point gain on Wednesday. The paper was 74 bid in late trading, players said.
Elsewhere, Marvel Holding's "old" bonds remained steady at 18-7/8 holding on to gains. Earlier in the week bonds traded at 17-1/4 bid, traders said.
The bonds have traded below 20 since Marvel and its holding companies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on December 27.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond was off 12/32 at 97-23/32 to yield 6.80 percent at the close.
